title: globally optimal embeddings for the sigmoid loss
PROPOSAL: We provide a proof of the global optimality of embeddings for the sigmoid loss, in the regime where both temperature and bias are trained together with the representations, assuming the dimension $d$ is fixed in advance and far from the number of data points $N$. In particular, we show that globally optimal embeddings have a specific aligned structure on the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, that aligns with existing results for $N \to \infty$. We also derive bounds for how quickly the loss value decreases as a function of $N$.
CONTROLS: We compare our results to the InfoNCE loss with fixed hyperparameters, and with a simple implementation of triplet loss.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our bounds will capture the dependence on $d$ and $N$ missed by prior works, which typically assumed either $d \ge N$ or $N \to \infty$. Moreover, our aligned structure of optimal embeddings will help provide new insights on the visual explanation of the modality gap phenomenon. However, it is unclear how tightly our optimality result will match the training process of practical models such as SigLIP, which adapt their hyperparameters over time.

title: comparing synaptic patterns of synchronization in siglip and openclip
PROPOSAL: We conduct an in-depth analysis of the synaptic patterns that emerge during the training process of SigLIP and OpenCLIP models, in particular by investigating how synapses adapt to synchronize representations across the text-image modalities. Our analysis focuses on exploring the matrix of inner products $U_i \cdot V_i$, where $U_i = f_\theta(X_i)$ and $V_i = g_\phi(Y_i)$, between all synchronizing representations. This analysis allows us to examine how synapses create alignment patterns in signal flow, facilitating effective synchronization and learning of the embedding space, which might help explain a decrease in modality gap under practice.
CONTROLS: We compare our results on the synaptic patterns to existing embeddings from fixed hyper-parameters on InfoNCE.
COST: 125 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the trajectories of synaptic patterns during training will reflect a shift towards alignments consistent with the structure described in prior theoretical work, despite possible transient deviations, and our analysis can provide valuable details on practical implementation and extension. However, more efficiently-designed models such as fixed-temperature SigLIP may present different characteristics.
